sheetsIndicative.note: two worksheets. Sheet 1 ('Report1646659776237') is the register snapshot: header Value,Status,Type then 150,181 data rows. Sheet 2 ('Sheet1') is a header-less single column of 36,526 callsigns, all of them a subset of sheet 1 and appearing in sheet 1's own row order (an order-preserving subsequence spanning all statuses); its purpose is not disclosed in the material. Both sheets are preserved verbatim as raw extracts; only sheet 1 is normalised into a dataset (see the raw-extract-sheet-2 declaration for why sheet 2 is not).

raw-extract-sheet-1-report1646659776237..contentsIndicative: mechanical extract of sheet 1; header Value,Status,Type then 150,181 rows. Status vocabulary Allocated (98,521), Reserved (51,271), Available (377) and blank (12); Type is 'Call Sign - Amateur' on every row. Anomalies preserved verbatim: one Value is literally ',,' (two commas) carrying a Reserved status; 'G6 FMU' has an interior space; three Values carry a trailing non-breaking space (G0TQK, G7IWE, 2E1HON); 479 four-character callsigns (two-letter-suffix heritage series) and 96 callsigns of six to nine characters, most of them reciprocal 'M/…' forms including curiosities such as M/M/PT2FM, M/#YO3IES, M/#VK4VGK and M/EI-8-DJ.

normalised--sheet-1-report1646659776237..contentsIndicative: header callsign,status,licence_class; 150,181 rows sorted by callsign (source order carries no meaning - not callsign-sorted, no dates). Status carried verbatim (Allocated/Reserved/Available and 12 blanks preserved); licence_class emitted empty (no class disclosed). The constant Type column is required-present but not carried. Three trailing non-breaking spaces were trimmed from callsigns (counted in the converter notes, never silent); the ',,' Value and the interior-space 'G6 FMU' are preserved verbatim. The ',,' callsign sorts first.

raw-extract-sheet-2-sheet1.csv.contentsIndicative: mechanical extract of sheet 2 ('Sheet1'): a header-less single column of 36,526 callsigns, all distinct and all present in sheet 1, appearing in sheet 1's own row order (an order-preserving subsequence). Their sheet-1 statuses are mixed (16,688 Allocated, 19,741 Reserved, 94 Available, 3 blank), so the column is not a clean status filter, and the workbook discloses no purpose for it. It asserts no status or attribute of its own, so normalising it would invent a set-membership the source does not explain: it is preserved verbatim here (required-present) but deliberately not converted into a normalised dataset. If its meaning is later established, a reviewed converter change can add it.
